Lemon Bot (web, macOS and iOS apps; separate product in the same repository)

claims.answer: Terminal TUI and one-shot CLI on macOS Apple Silicon and Linux (glibc 2.39+); Phoenix browser workspace with phone-width layout; Telegram and Discord text channels; Lemon Bot (separate product) with React web, macOS and iOS SwiftUI apps. Native Windows, macOS Intel and Android are unsupported or absent; the Mac DMG is unpublished.

scope.plan: Open source (MIT), self-hosted; user pays model providers and hosts

desktop_os.answer: Prebuilt releases for Apple Silicon macOS and Linux x86_64/ARM64 (glibc 2.39+); macOS Intel and native Windows have no builds; the Lemon Bot Mac app builds from source and the signed DMG is unpublished.

mobile_apps.answer: Lemon Bot has a SwiftUI iOS app (QR pairing, camera, share extension) with App Store release tooling; no Android app; Telegram/Discord are other phone routes.

browser.answer: `lemon web` Phoenix workspace (diffs, tool cards, automation boards, usage, command palette) and the Lemon Bot React web app.

mobile_browser.answer: Web workspace has responsive layouts down to phone width and Bot web is a responsive workspace; docs/user-guide/phone-acceptance.md covers phone acceptance.

cli.answer: `lemon` TUI, `lemon -p ... --output json|stream-json`, and many subcommands (doctor, sessions, omp, mcp, backup, update).

editor_extensions.answer: No IDE extension; Tern panes and ACP chat surface editor locations, and a browser-node extension exists for browser automation.

task_actions.answer: Start, follow-up, steer, redirect, cancel, resume and approve from TUI, web and Telegram/Discord (/steer, /cancel, /resume, approval buttons).

notifications.answer: Telegram/Discord messages, Bot Web Push/APNs and heartbeats; TUI shows approval notifications.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Sessions persist in the daemon and are reachable from every surface (start on Telegram, review in web).

limitations: Prebuilt releases only for Apple Silicon macOS and Linux; Mac/iOS Bot apps are built from source or pending distribution; no Android app.

claims.answer: Lemon runs its own native agent for every top-level run (engine "lemon" is provenance only), spawns native child sessions, and can delegate to omp (oh-my-pi) as an external agent; vendor harness engines (Claude Code, Codex) are not selectable. Models come from many providers.

harnesses.answer: Native Lemon agent is the only top-level executor; omp is a delegate driver ("not Lemon engine"); historical vendor resume tokens cannot select or resume top-level execution.

session_integration.answer: Embedded harness (coding_agent via lemon_agent/lemon_ai) and omp controlled over its structured RPC protocol (omp --mode rpc).

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Lemon native sessions and omp sessions are two different harnesses that Lemon can run, monitor and steer in one workspace.

limitations: Only one embedded harness plus omp delegation; no Claude Code/Codex/Cursor harness.

claims.answer: Sign in with a ChatGPT or Claude Pro/Max subscription (and copy an existing Codex CLI login with consent), bring API keys for many providers, or use local models; no vendor credits.

changes.summary: Independent review correction: RUN-02 said there is no per-task container option, but the source has an optional Docker terminal backend for exec/process shell commands (isolation :container, network none by default).

before.answer: Runs execute in the project directory as the host user; kanban tasks and omp workers can use managed per-task git worktrees. Tool policy and approvals are enforced, but docs state there is no OS filesystem, process or network sandbox; WASM runtime exists for tools.

after.answer: Runs execute in the project directory as the host user by default; kanban tasks and omp workers can use managed per-task git worktrees, and the exec/process shell tools can optionally run commands in a Docker container backend (cwd mounted at /workspace, read-only root, network none by default, CPU/memory/pids limits; default backend is local; applies to shell commands, not the whole run). Tool policy and approvals are enforced, but docs state there is no OS-level sandbox for the host run; WASM runtime exists for tools.
